earlier_scan.source_named: Blust, Robert 2007, 'Oma Longh historical phonology', Oceanic Linguistics 46 — paywalled; Soriente 2006 text collection also names the variety

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (rev. ed.). Asia-Pacific Linguistics 8. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 4.1.3, p. 186 (Borneo sound systems); Òma Lóngh named only in sec. 9.2.2.4 pp. 669-670 (rounding of final *a).
sources.note: Areal only: 'Unlike the Philippines, stress is not phonemic in any language of Borneo. However, unlike much of the AN world, where stress falls predictably on the penult, many of the languages of coastal Sarawak, and some interior languages have final stress in citation forms, but penultimate stress in phrasal context.' Òma Lóngh not named; its only mentions concern final *a > -o.
